_comment: The single place the native apps get their identity from. Read by capacitor.config.ts, by android/app/build.gradle, and by scripts/mobile-identity.mjs, so an identifier can never be right in one project and wrong in the other. NOT YET REGISTERED with either store — see `registered` below.
_appName_comment: The name that appears under the icon on a phone's home screen, and nowhere else. It is title-cased — Hangyul Ganada — because a launcher label sits beside Photos, Maps and Settings, and a lowercased second word reads there as a typo rather than as the deliberate lowercase of 가나다. The prose product name in the app, the store listing and every document stays `Hangyul ganada`; scripts/check-product-name.mjs enforces that split, and scripts/check-mobile-identity.mjs enforces that Android's strings.xml and iOS's Info.plist both carry exactly this value. Changing the name here and nowhere else is the supported way to rename the installed app.

registered._comment: Set each to true only once the identifier has actually been created in the corresponding console. Nothing in the build depends on these; they exist so the release checklist cannot be answered from memory.

_version_comment: 1.0.4. The previous release was content — a Numbers lesson and a set of corrections — and the version name stayed still for it, which was right. This one is not. The Vocabulary Level Test chooses its questions differently: it opens on a warm-up ladder instead of at level 14, moves by at most three levels between questions, and stops between twenty and thirty items rather than always at thirty, so the intro screen makes a different promise in all thirty-two languages. Its item bank changed at every level: no dictionary headword is asked below level 11 any more, which removes the level-1 question whose correct answer was "nougat". A sitting is now written to the device and survives the app being closed, which is a new stored field and schema 14. A learner who updates will see the test behave differently on the first sitting after it, and that is what a version name is for.
_buildNumber_comment: 17, because 16 is spent. The delivered AAB and APK in result/ and app_result/ both report versionCode 16 and build-info.json records 16, and product files have changed since the commit that produced them — the level-test engine, its item bank in all thirty-two languages, the persisted schema, and one string in each of the thirty-two interface bundles. A rebuild at 16 would put different bytes under a code a set of bytes already exists for. `npm run version:check` is what said so, before the build rather than after. Nothing has been uploaded to Play (see `registered.googlePlay`), so 17 is the next valid code rather than the next unused one. This number is set by a person deciding to ship, never incremented by a script or a tool run.

android._comment: targetSdk 36 because Google Play requires Android 16 for new apps and updates from 31 August 2026. minSdk 24 is Capacitor 8's floor and covers ~99% of active devices.

xcode._comment: What `App.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` currently carries, written down here so that a check can tell a *deliberate lag* from a *drift*. The Xcode project is maintained on a Mac, by hand, through the Xcode UI: MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION are build settings Xcode owns, and editing them from Linux with a text substitution is how a project file loses a setting it was never asked about. So this release moves Android to 1.0.4 build 17 and leaves iOS where its maintainer left it. `scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs` asserts the project file matches these two values exactly — any other change to it fails — and prints the pending action while they are behind `version` and `buildNumber`.
xcode.pending: iOS is behind: set MARKETING_VERSION to 1.0.4 and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION to 17 in Xcode (App target, both configurations), then update the two values above in the same commit. The project file is not edited from here — see the comment above.

ios._comment: 15.0 to match IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET in the Xcode project — the two disagreeing is how a build succeeds and then crashes on a device the store said it supported. Capacitor 8's own floor is 14; 15 is chosen because it is what the project is configured for and covers every device Apple still updates. Apple requires builds made with the iOS 26 SDK from 28 April 2026; that is the SDK you build *with*, not the version you deploy *to*.
